subject: Recap & next steps: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification (PriorityHealth)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@priorityhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification (PriorityHealth)

Hi Jake — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared baseline and clear next steps. Please correct anything I get wrong.

Summary from call:
- Expected monthly token volume: ~1.2B tokens (PriorityHealth estimate from current forecasts / pilot traffic).
- Typical/avg sustained throughput implied: ~460 tokens/sec; expected peak bursts up to ~1.4–1.6k tokens/sec.
- Target latency: 200–400ms for 250–1k token responses; concurrency target ~8–12 parallel requests.
- Workload: production inference for summarization + contextual QA across patient support chat and clinician notes (prefix caching will help).
- Compliance/ops: you need Private/Dedicated with VPC and audit logs; procurement will own contractual flow.

Dedicated capacity considerations we discussed:
- GPU preference: you said latency-sensitive workloads and willingness to evaluate H100; A100 is an alternative if committed capacity needs to be larger.
- Reservation length: you indicated preference for a 12-month committed plan if numbers work.

Initial pricing posture (high level) — we'll surface exact model-specifics in the attached pricing sheet but wanted to align on the unit economics you’re targeting: 
- Target $/1M tokens (your ask): $15–$18 per 1M tokens as a realistic target for H100-backed reserved capacity (higher throughput / lower per-token).
- If you prefer A100-based cluster (higher GPU count for same throughput), expected unit will be higher (we estimated ~$25–$30 per 1M tokens).

Immediate next steps / asks:
1) Can you confirm the 1.2B tokens/month and peak throughput numbers, or share the spreadsheet if you want us to run alternate load scenarios? (I attached a template: PriorityHealth_Monthly_Estimates.xlsx)
2) Confirm procurement contact and PO timeline so we can align SOW cadence.
3) Would you be open to a short technical validation call with our infra team to validate the throughput targets (30 min)?

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_Sheet_v3.pdf (pricing scenarios), PriorityHealth_Monthly_Estimates.xlsx (your numbers template).

If those numbers look right I’ll put together two concrete committed-plan options (H100-focused and A100-focused) with monthly price and $/1M token unit economics.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification (PriorityHealth)

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Monthly tokens: yes, 1.2B is our working forecast for Q1 after rollout to our support cohorts. We can share a breakdown (by feature) in the attached spreadsheet — I filled the sheet and re-attached.
- Peak throughput: our load tests show bursts near 1.5k tokens/sec; sustained baseline closer to 450 tps.
- Latency: H100 is preferred (we care about 200–300ms P95). If H100 pricing is too high we can consider A100 but performance is first priority.
- Target $/1M tokens: we'd like to be in the $15–$18 range as you noted. Budget range for a committed plan is roughly $20k–$35k/month depending on SLA and support.

Procurement: procurement@priorityhealth.com is on copy — their timeline is typically 2–3 weeks to approve standard SOWs and PO once pricing is agreed.

We’re happy to run a technical call; rishi/neha can coordinate the date. Thanks for the quick follow-up.

—Jake
Jake Turner
Head of ML Products | PriorityHealth

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, PriorityHealth Procurement <procurement@priorityhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification (PriorityHealth)

Great — thanks for the filled sheet, Jake. Based on your confirmed volumes and preference for H100, I ran two candidate committed plans (high level) so you have concrete unit economics to review. Full line-item pricing is in the attached Redwood_Dedicated_Pricing_Sheet_v3.pdf. Short summary below: 

Plan A — H100-focused (recommended for latency-sensitive production)
- Reserved capacity: 4 x H100 (pre-warmed pool)
- Expected aggregate throughput: up to ~2.0k tokens/sec sustained with headroom for bursts (depends on model size/quantization).
- Estimated monthly price (12-mo commit): $28,500 / month (includes SLA & 24/7 support)
- Implied unit economics: ~ $15 / 1M tokens (assumes 75% utilization of the reserved cluster vs the 1.2B token run-rate).

Plan B — A100-focused (lower GPU sku, larger footprint)
- Reserved capacity: 8 x A100
- Expected aggregate throughput: ~1.6k tokens/sec sustained (good for batch-y workloads, slightly higher latency P95).
- Estimated monthly price (12-mo commit): $36,000 / month
- Implied unit economics: ~ $30 / 1M tokens (assumes similar utilization and higher ops amortization).

Notes/assumptions: 
- Unit economics above are simplified (we amortized reserved GPU cost + fixed infra & support across expected utilization). If utilization rises above 75% the $/1M improves materially.
- We can run a short dedicated proof-of-performance (1-week) on 2 x H100 as a validation step; if you sign a 12-mo commit we can apply a credit for the trial.
- Pricing sheet includes model family assumptions (LLM size, tokenization overhead) and optional add-ons (extended retention, SOC2 evidence package).

Proposed next steps:
1) Schedule 30-min infra validation call (Rishi will lead technical Q&A). Suggested times: Thu 12/03 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 12/04 14:00–15:00 PT — which works for you?
2) If Plan A looks good, we’ll prepare a draft SOW and a DocuSign-ready SOW (I’ve attached RDW_SOW_draft_PriorityHealth_v1.docx).
3) Procurement: if timeline is 2–3 weeks, we’ll target start-of-service on 2027-01-04 pending SOW/PO.

If you want, I can also run a sensitivity table showing $/1M at 60/75/90% utilization — I included the sample in the pricing PDF.

Looking forward to the infra call.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Marissa / Jake — thanks for the detailed options. Procurement here — a few quick process notes: 
- Timeline: once we have an agreed pricing plan we typically need ~10 business days to review SOW and issue PO for standard terms.
- Required items: final SOW, pricing sheet, SOC2 attestation (if included in the SOW), and an invoice remit/AR contact.
- Payment terms: standard is Net 30; if Redwood offers Net 45 or early-pay discount we can consider.

We’ll review Plan A (H100) internally; next immediate ask is for a clean SOW/DocuSign link we can route. Please send the DocuSign URL (or upload to our shared procurement portal).

Thanks — procurement@priorityhealth.com
